title: Review: Muscle and motility; Adaptation to environment; Ecological niches

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Community
items.clue: All the populations of different species living and interacting in the same area.

items.label: Realized niche
items.clue: The actual extent of a species' niche when it is in competition with other species.

items.label: Obligate anaerobe
items.clue: An organism that can grow only where oxygen gas is absent from its environment; oxygen is toxic to it, so it cannot tolerate aerobic conditions.

items.label: Fundamental niche
items.clue: The potential niche of a species: the full range of conditions and resources it could use, based on its adaptations and tolerance limits, in the absence of competition from other species.

questions.stem: Which statement gives the meaning of the term habitat as it is used in ecology?

options.text: The place in which a community, species, population or single organism lives.
The role that a species plays in its ecosystem, including what it feeds on.
A large region of the Earth that shares one type of climate, such as tundra.
The set of organisms of different species that live together in one area.

questions.explanation: This is the definition used in the guide. A habitat is a place, and it can be the place where a whole community lives or where one organism lives; it is described by geographical location, physical location and ecosystem type.

questions.stem: Which statement about abiotic variables and the distribution of species is correct?

options.text: Only the distribution of plants is limited by abiotic variables, because animals are able to move away from unfavourable conditions.
A species with a wide range of tolerance for temperature is found everywhere that the temperature lies within that range.
Adaptations give a species a range of tolerance for each abiotic variable, and it is absent where a variable is outside that range.
An abiotic variable is any feature of the environment, whether it is living or non-living, that differs between one place and another.

questions.stem: Students are required to collect transect data from a natural or semi-natural habitat. Which of these sites is semi-natural?

options.text: A hay meadow that is cut once each year but is dominated by wild grasses and wildflowers.
A field of wheat grown from sown seed, with wild poppies growing along its margins.
A garden lawn sown with a bought seed mixture and mown every week through the summer.
A peat bog in a remote upland with no history of drainage, grazing or other management.

questions.stem: Which statement about the conditions needed for a coral reef to form is correct?

options.text: The water must be deep, so that the coral polyps are shielded from the damaging effects of bright sunlight.
The water should be turbid and rich in suspended sediment, which supplies food to the polyps.
The water must be shallow and clear enough for light to reach the zooxanthellae in the coral tissue.
The water should be as warm as possible, because calcification speeds up with every rise in temperature.

questions.stem: A biome has long, very cold winters, a growing season of only a few weeks, precipitation below about 250 mm a year and permanently frozen subsoil. Which biome is this?

options.text: Taiga, as in northern Canada
Hot desert, as in Arabia
Tundra, as in Arctic Canada
Grassland, as on the prairies

questions.explanation: Very cold temperatures, a growing season of a few weeks, very low precipitation and permafrost are the climate conditions that characterize tundra, which supports low-growing plants but no trees.

questions.stem: What is meant by the ecological niche of a species?

options.text: The role of the species in its ecosystem, including its biotic and abiotic interactions
The place where the species lives, described by its location and ecosystem type
The position of the species in a food chain, defined by the food it eats
The interactions of the species with other organisms, leaving out abiotic factors

questions.explanation: This is the guide's definition. A niche is a role, described by the biotic and abiotic interactions that influence the species' growth, survival and reproduction, including how it obtains food.

questions.stem: Which statement describes an obligate anaerobe?

options.text: An organism that does not use oxygen but is unharmed when oxygen gas is present
An organism that normally respires anaerobically but can use oxygen if needed
An organism that can grow only where oxygen gas is absent from its environment
An organism that switches to anaerobic respiration when its oxygen supply runs out

questions.explanation: Obligate anaerobes cannot tolerate oxygen gas. They are found only in oxygen-free environments, such as deep sediments or the gut, because oxygen prevents their growth.

questions.stem: In which groups of organisms is photosynthesis the mode of nutrition?

options.text: Plants, algae and several groups of photosynthetic prokaryotes such as cyanobacteria
Plants and algae only, because prokaryotes are unable to photosynthesize
Plants, algae and any prokaryotes whose cells happen to contain chloroplasts
Plants, algae and photosynthetic prokaryotes, though plants also feed from the soil

questions.explanation: Photosynthesis is the mode of nutrition of plants, of algae and of several groups of photosynthetic prokaryotes. All synthesize their own carbon compounds from carbon dioxide using light energy.

questions.stem: Which statement about nutrition in animals is correct?

options.text: Animals that host photosynthetic algae inside their cells are autotrophic
Animals assimilate their food by absorbing it across the lining of the gut
Animals are heterotrophs that ingest, digest, absorb and assimilate food
Animals ingest food when digested molecules pass into their cells

questions.explanation: All animals are heterotrophic. Their holozoic nutrition consists of ingestion of food, internal digestion, absorption of the products and their assimilation into the animal's tissues.

options.text: Secretion of enzymes onto dead organic matter, followed by absorption of the products of digestion
Ingestion of dead organic matter, followed by internal digestion and absorption of products
Any feeding on dead organic matter, whether by fungi and bacteria or by earthworms and woodlice
Synthesis of carbon compounds by fungi and bacteria that grow on dead organic matter

questions.stem: How were biologists able to deduce the diets of extinct hominids such as Paranthropus robustus?

options.text: By developing theories relating dentition to diet from the fossils themselves, then confirming them with living mammals
By comparing the size of the fossil jaws with those of living carnivores, since powerful jaws indicate meat-eating
By treating the question as unanswerable, since the diet of an extinct animal is a guess that cannot be tested
By applying theories relating dentition to diet, developed from observing living mammals, to the fossil teeth

questions.stem: Shrubs and herbs grow on the floor of a forest beneath a closed canopy. How do these plants obtain enough light to survive?

options.text: They are shade tolerant, able to photosynthesize at the low light intensities reaching the floor
They obtain carbon compounds from the decaying leaf litter, so they need little light
They receive sugar from the canopy trees through underground fungal networks
They cannot; plants that fail to reach the canopy survive only until they are shaded

questions.stem: Which set of features of a dolphin reduces drag as it swims, and so is an adaptation for streamlining?

options.text: A spindle-shaped body with the hind limbs lost, no external ears, almost no hair and an outline smoothed by a layer of blubber under the skin.
A thick layer of blubber that insulates the body; it makes the outline bulkier, but the extra drag is overcome by the powerful fluke.
A body made less dense by blubber and large lungs, so that the dolphin floats and does not have to push against the water as it swims.
Flippers and a fluke that are fins of the same kind as a fish's, replacing the limbs of a land mammal so that they cut through the water.
